correctness.rationale: For any admissible P, the centered spectral progress is no greater than the infimum Rayleigh quotient of I−P on 1⊥. A vector constant on each bulk has energy only at the three effective links A,c,B; minimizing over the gateways gives R(U−V)², while the centered norm squared is at least the bulk-only variance (U−V)²/s. A zero link gives a disconnection and zero progress, so the bound extends to boundary weights. The inequalities A,B≤1−c and (g−f(c))(1+c)=(c−c*)² give the bridge bound; the resistance difference 1/R−1/f(c) is at least the gateway holding sum, giving its claimed bound. The proposed stochastic kernel has two bulk zero-sum eigenvalues −x/n and −x/r and the given four-state quotient. Testing its variance at the bulk barycenter yields a Poincaré constant ≤1/(gs)+2/x+2/g≤1/(gs)+C/g. For n,r≥4 the quotient perturbation norm relative to the isolated bulks plus central block is ≤3x/4; the second eigenvalue is ≥1−gs from the same path test and lies strictly above all negative magnitudes and the other nontrivial modes. This verifies the finite sandwich for SLEM rather than just a one-sided gap. Compactness ensures attainment; substituting the sandwich gives the bounds for every optimizer. With balanced growing sizes the same comparison gives d(P)/s→R(c,h), and α=2g/(1−c*)²=1 gives R(c*,h)/g=1−h+O(h²), while the vanishing-holding loss is exactly quadratic from the displayed identity. Taking size large before sending the perturbation to zero establishes exponent sharpness, not tight finite constants.
residual_risks: The proof's Rayleigh gap is the infimum on 1⊥ (possibly zero), not the smallest strictly positive eigenvalue in a reducible case; the zero-link test still gives the claimed bound.
The lower construction uses both clique orders ≥5; arbitrary nonreversible chains and exact optimizer-face classification are out of scope.
